question: The revolutionary Bagha Jatin (Jatindranath Mukherjee) was known for his valiant fight and for inspiring revolutionaries in which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Bagha Jatin**, also known as **Jatindranath Mukherjee**, was a prominent revolutionary leader during the Indian freedom struggle.

• He hailed from the state of **Bengal**, which played a pivotal role in the revolutionary activities against British rule.

• Bagha Jatin earned his moniker "Bagha" (meaning tiger) after he killed a tiger single-handedly in **1906**, showcasing his unparalleled bravery.

• He was a key figure in organizing revolutionary groups in **Bengal**, including the **Jugantar Party**, which actively worked against British imperialism.

• Bagha Jatin's valiant fight against the British forces in **1915** at **Balasore, Odisha**, remains one of the most heroic episodes of India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Bengal's Role in Revolutionary Activities:**

• **Bengal** emerged as a hub for revolutionary activities during the early 20th century due to widespread dissatisfaction with British policies like the **Partition of Bengal in 1905**.

• Several revolutionary organizations such as the **Jugantar** and **Anushilan Samiti** were established in Bengal to challenge British authority.

• Prominent revolutionaries like **Bagha Jatin, Surya Sen, Khudiram Bose, and Prafulla Chaki** hailed from Bengal and contributed significantly to India's independence movement.

• **Life and Legacy of Bagha Jatin:**

• **Born:** Jatin was born on **7 December 1879** in **Kushtia, Bengal Presidency** (now in Bangladesh).

• He was deeply influenced by **Swami Vivekananda**, who inspired him to dedicate his life to the service of the nation.

• Jatin played a crucial role in procuring arms and organizing revolutionary activities aimed at overthrowing British rule.

• His famous last words, "Amra morbo, jagat jagbe" (We shall die so that the world may awaken), reflect his selfless sacrifice for the nation.

• **Other States in the Context of Revolutionaries:**

• **Punjab:** Punjab was known for revolutionaries like **Bhagat Singh, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Udham Singh**, who played pivotal roles in India's struggle for freedom.

• **Uttar Pradesh:** Uttar Pradesh was home to leaders like **Chandrashekhar Azad** and served as a significant center for revolutionary activities, including the Kakori Train Robbery.

• **Bihar:** Bihar contributed leaders like **Jayaprakash Narayan** and revolutionary activities during the Quit India Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Jugantar Party:** Founded in **1906**, this revolutionary group aimed to overthrow British rule through armed resistance.

• **Partition of Bengal (1905):** A British policy aimed at dividing Bengal along religious lines, which led to widespread protests and the rise of revolutionary movements.

• **Balasore Battle (1915):** Bagha Jatin and his associates fought valiantly against British forces but were ultimately outnumbered and defeated, leading to Jatin's martyrdom.

• **Legacy:** Jatin's life continues to inspire generations of Indians, symbolizing courage and patriotism in the face of oppression.
